original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: For seed 5, exhaustively test jointly boundary-adaptive frame choices for PR589 A operation 2071 and B operation 820 at shared register 659, then price every legal pair.
scope_change_reason: No catalogue card names this transport follow-up. The bit-helper-contract card is retained as the nearest bit-track catalogue anchor only; the actual investigation is the independent PR #1382 open question on reciprocal A/B boundary adaptation.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper A/B transport pair could reduce the bit supplier cost in the selected assembly, but the current accepted result is complex-limited; this is a scoped side result and does not alter the selected kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after exhausting every exact commutation slot region for the two named operations and every stage-local catalog/closure frame candidate; restore both reciprocal stage boundaries, COPY constraints and full touched-register chains for each pair.
evidence: Exact rational census on the pinned PR589 word: 20 dynamically generated assignments, 12 pass both boundaries and complete chains, 8 fail the reciprocal A upper bound; passing profiles are 8 ties and 4 strict losses, with no improvements/unresolved cases. The fixed-boundary control has the same 12 valid pairs; all 12 legal pairs is replayed through wlib.rebuild_C and wlib.paid.
author: Cinna Davis
